Now I have a comprehensive picture. Let me compile everything into my report.

Here is my thorough analysis of how course content is structured in the tutors project.

---

## 1. Existing Test/Example Course Content in the Repo

**There is no test course, example course, sample course, or any course content in this repository.** No `tutors.json`, `properties.yaml`, or `course.md` files exist anywhere in the repo. No `python-101` directory exists either. This repo is purely the **Reader** application -- it consumes course JSON from external URLs, it does not contain course source material.

The README at `D:\code\tutors\README.md` (lines 29-39) explains the architecture:
- **Generator** (separate repo `tutors-sdk/tutors-apps`): transforms a folder of learning content into a `tutors.json` file
- **Reader** (this repo): presents a Tutors course by fetching `tutors.json` from a URL

---

## 2. How tutors.json Works -- Structure and Format

The Reader fetches `tutors.json` from a URL like `https://<course-id>.netlify.app/tutors.json`. The loading code is at `D:\code\tutors\src\lib\services\course\services\course.svelte.ts` (line 37):

```typescript
const response = await fetchFunction(`${courseProtocol.value}${courseUrl}/tutors.json`);
const data = await response.json();
course = data as Course;
decorateCourseTree(course, courseId, courseUrl);
```

### Minimal tutors.json Structure

Based on the live reference course at `https://reference-course.netlify.app/tutors.json`, the JSON has this shape:

**Top-level (Course) object:**
```json
{
  "route": "/",
  "type": "course",
  "title": "Reference Course",
  "summary": "Short description",
  "contentMd": "# Reference Course\n\nMarkdown content...",
  "frontMatter": {},
  "id": "repo",
  "img": "https://{{COURSEURL}}/course.png",
  "imgFile": "course.png",
  "video": "",
  "videoids": {"videoid": "", "videoIds": []},
  "hide": false,
  "authLevel": 0,
  "los": [ /* array of Topic objects */ ],
  "properties": { /* from properties.yaml */ }
}
```

**Topic object (inside `los`):**
```json
{
  "route": "/topic/{{COURSEURL}}/topic-01-typical",
  "type": "topic",
  "title": "Simple",
  "summary": "Units with presentations, labs + resources",
  "contentMd": "# Simple\n\nUnits with presentations, labs + resources\n",
  "frontMatter": {},
  "id": "topic-01-typical",
  "img": "https://{{COURSEURL}}/topic-01-typical/typical.png",
  "imgFile": "typical.png",
  "video": "",
  "videoids": {"videoid": "", "videoIds": []},
  "hide": false,
  "authLevel": 0,
  "los": [ /* array of Unit objects */ ]
}
```

**Unit object (inside a topic's `los`):**
```json
{
  "route": "/topic/{{COURSEURL}}/topic-01-typical/",
  "type": "unit",
  "title": "Main Lesson",
  "summary": "",
  "contentMd": "Main Lesson\n",
  "frontMatter": {},
  "id": "unit-1",
  "img": "", "imgFile": "",
  "video": "",
  "videoids": {"videoid": "", "videoIds": []},
  "hide": false,
  "authLevel": 0,
  "los": [ /* Talks, Labs, Notes, etc. */ ]
}
```

**Talk object:**
```json
{
  "route": "/talk/{{COURSEURL}}/topic-01-typical/unit-1/talk-1-intro",
  "type": "talk",
  "title": "Lecture 1",
  "summary": "A short summary...",
  "contentMd": "Lecture 1\n\nA short summary...",
  "frontMatter": {},
  "id": "talk-1-intro",
  "img": "https://{{COURSEURL}}/topic-01-typical/unit-1/talk-1-intro/introduction.png",
  "imgFile": "introduction.png",
  "video": "",
  "videoids": {"videoid": "", "videoIds": []},
  "hide": false,
  "authLevel": 0,
  "pdf": "https://{{COURSEURL}}/topic-01-typical/unit-1/talk-1-intro/introduction.pdf",
  "pdfFile": "introduction.pdf"
}
```

**Lab object (with steps):**
```json
{
  "route": "/lab/{{COURSEURL}}/topic-01-typical/unit-1/book-a",
  "type": "lab",
  "title": "Lab-01",
  "summary": "A set of practical instructions...",
  "contentMd": "# Objectives\n\nA set of practical instructions...\n",
  "frontMatter": {},
  "id": "book-a",
  "img": "https://{{COURSEURL}}/topic-01-typical/unit-1/book-a/img/main.png",
  "imgFile": "img/main.png",
  "video": "",
  "videoids": {"videoid": "", "videoIds": []},
  "hide": false,
  "authLevel": 0,
  "los": [
    {
      "title": "Objectives",
      "shortTitle": "Lab-01",
      "contentMd": "# Objectives\n\nContent...\n",
      "route": "/lab/{{COURSEURL}}/topic-01-typical/unit-1/book-a/Lab-01",
      "id": "Lab-01",
      "type": "step"
    }
  ]
}
```

The `{{COURSEURL}}` placeholder is replaced at runtime by `injectCourseUrl()` in `D:\code\tutors\src\lib\services\course\services\lo-tree.ts` (lines 114-143). For routes, it is replaced with the `courseId`; for images and PDFs, it is replaced with the `courseUrl` (the domain).

### Properties Object

The `properties` key on the course object comes from `properties.yaml` in the source course. It is a flat key-value map. The `loadPropertyFlags()` function in `D:\code\tutors\node_modules\@tutors\tutors-model-lib\src\utils\course-utils.ts` (lines 135-172) reads these keys:
- `portfolio` (boolean), `private` (number 0/1), `auth` (number), `llm` (number)
- `hideVideos` (boolean), `labStepsAutoNumber` (boolean)
- `footer` (string), `defaultPdfReader` (string), `pdfOrientation` (string)
- `ignorepin` (string), `icon` (object with `type` and `color`)
- `slack`, `zoom`, `moodle`, `youtube`, `teams`, `podcast` -- URLs for companion links
- `companions` -- custom companion links with icon definitions

## 3. Course Generator / Builder / CLI Tool

The generator is in a **separate repository**: `https://github.com/tutors-sdk/tutors-apps`

Its structure:
```
tutors-apps/
  cli/
    tutors-model-lib/       -- Shared type definitions (published to JSR)
    tutors-gen-lib/         -- Course generation logic
    tutors-publish/         -- Primary CLI: folder -> tutors.json
    tutors-publish-html/    -- Alternative: folder -> static HTML site
    tutors-publish-npm/     -- npm compatibility wrapper
```

This reader project consumes the model library as a dependency. From `D:\code\tutors\package.json` (line 57):
```
"@tutors/tutors-model-lib": "npm:@jsr/tutors__tutors-model-lib@^5.0.0"
```

The README at `D:\code\tutors\README.md` (lines 169-175) notes for debugging you can point to a local copy:
```

```

## 4. python-101 Directory

## 5. How decorateCourseTree and flattenLos Parse JSON

### Type Hierarchy (from `D:\code\tutors\node_modules\@tutors\tutors-model-lib\src\types\learning-objects.ts`)

```
Lo (base type)
  |-- Lab (type: "lab", has los: LabStep[], pdf, pdfFile)
  |-- Talk (type: "talk", has pdf, pdfFile)
  |-- Archive (type: "archive", has archiveFile)
  |-- Web (type: "web")
  |-- Github (type: "github")
  |-- Tutorial (type: "tutorial", has pdf, pdfFile)
  |-- Note (type: "note")
  |-- Podcast (type: "podcast", has episode)
  |-- PanelNote (type: "panelnote")
  |-- PanelTalk (type: "paneltalk", extends Talk)
  |-- PanelVideo (type: "panelvideo")
  |-- Composite (extends Lo, has toc: Lo[], los: Lo[], panels: Panels, units: Units)
      |-- Topic (type: "topic")
      |-- Unit (type: "unit")
      |-- Side (type: "side")
      |-- Course (type: "course", has courseId, courseUrl, topicIndex, loIndex, walls, wallMap, properties, calendar, enrollment, ...)
```

### Common Lo fields:
- `type`, `id`, `title`, `summary`, `contentMd`, `frontMatter`, `contentHtml`
- `route`, `authLevel`, `img`, `imgFile`, `icon`
- `video`, `videoids`, `hide`
- `parentLo`, `parentTopic`, `parentCourse`, `breadCrumbs` (set at runtime)

### Simple vs Composite types (from `D:\code\tutors\node_modules\@tutors\tutors-model-lib\src\types\type-utils.ts`):
- **Simple types**: note, archive, web, github, panelnote, paneltalk, panelvideo, podcast, talk, book, lab, tutorial
- **Composite types**: unit, side, topic, course

### flattenLos (from `D:\code\tutors\node_modules\@tutors\tutors-model-lib\src\utils\lo-utils.ts`, lines 22-33):
Recursively walks the tree. For each Lo, pushes it to results, then if it has a `los` property (i.e., is composite), recursively flattens those children too. Returns a flat array of all Los in the course.

### decorateCourseTree (from `D:\code\tutors\node_modules\@tutors\tutors-model-lib\src\services\lo-tree.ts`, lines 7-43):
1. Sets `courseId`, `courseUrl`, and `route` on the course
2. Flattens all Los and injects the course URL (replacing `{{COURSEURL}}` placeholders)
3. Removes unknown Los
4. Calls `decorateLoTree` recursively which:
   - Sets `parentCourse` on every Lo
   - Loads icon from frontMatter
   - Builds breadcrumbs
   - Converts markdown to HTML
   - For composite Los: extracts `panels` (panelVideos, panelTalks, panelNotes, podcasts) and `units` (units, sides, standardLos), builds `toc`, then recurses into children
5. Builds `loIndex` (Map of route -> Lo) and `topicIndex` (Map of route -> Topic)
6. Calls `loadPropertyFlags`, `createCompanions`, `createWalls`, `initCalendar`

## 1. Existing Test/Example Course Content in the Repo

**There is no test course, example course, sample course, or any course content in this repository.** No `tutors.json`, `properties.yaml`, or `course.md` files exist anywhere in the repo. ## 2. How tutors.json Works -- Structure and Format

The Reader fetches `tutors.json` from a URL like `https://<course-id>.netlify.app/tutors.json`. The loading code is at `D:\code\tutors\src\lib\services\course\services\course.svelte.ts` (line 37):

```typescript
const response = await fetchFunction(`${courseProtocol.value}${courseUrl}/tutors.json`);
const data = await response.json();
course = data as Course;
decorateCourseTree(course, courseId, courseUrl);
```

### Properties Object

The `properties` key on the course object comes from `properties.yaml` in the source course. It is a flat key-value map. The `loadPropertyFlags()` function in `D:\code\tutors\node_modules\@tutors\tutors-model-lib\src\utils\course-utils.ts` (lines 135-172) reads these keys:
- `portfolio` (boolean), `private` (number 0/1), `auth` (number), `llm` (number)
- `hideVideos` (boolean), `labStepsAutoNumber` (boolean)
- `footer` (string), `defaultPdfReader` (string), `pdfOrientation` (string)
- `ignorepin` (string), `icon` (object with `type` and `color`)
- `slack`, `zoom`, `moodle`, `youtube`, `teams`, `podcast` -- URLs for companion links
- `companions` -- custom companion links with icon definitions

## 5. How decorateCourseTree and flattenLos Parse JSON

### Type Hierarchy (from `D:\code\tutors\node_modules\@tutors\tutors-model-lib\src\types\learning-objects.ts`)

```
Lo (base type)
  |-- Lab (type: "lab", has los: LabStep[], pdf, pdfFile)
  |-- Talk (type: "talk", has pdf, pdfFile)
  |-- Archive (type: "archive", has archiveFile)
  |-- Web (type: "web")
  |-- Github (type: "github")
  |-- Tutorial (type: "tutorial", has pdf, pdfFile)
  |-- Note (type: "note")
  |-- Podcast (type: "podcast", has episode)
  |-- PanelNote (type: "panelnote")
  |-- PanelTalk (type: "paneltalk", extends Talk)
  |-- PanelVideo (type: "panelvideo")
  |-- Composite (extends Lo, has toc: Lo[], los: Lo[], panels: Panels, units: Units)
      |-- Topic (type: "topic")
      |-- Unit (type: "unit")
      |-- Side (type: "side")
      |-- Course (type: "course", has courseId, courseUrl, topicIndex, loIndex, walls, wallMap, properties, calendar, enrollment, ...)
```

### Common Lo fields:
- `type`, `id`, `title`, `summary`, `contentMd`, `frontMatter`, `contentHtml`
- `route`, `authLevel`, `img`, `imgFile`, `icon`
- `video`, `videoids`, `hide`
- `parentLo`, `parentTopic`, `parentCourse`, `breadCrumbs` (set at runtime)

### Simple vs Composite types (from `D:\code\tutors\node_modules\@tutors\tutors-model-lib\src\types\type-utils.ts`):
- **Simple types**: note, archive, web, github, panelnote, paneltalk, panelvideo, podcast, talk, book, lab, tutorial
- **Composite types**: unit, side, topic, course

### flattenLos (from `D:\code\tutors\node_modules\@tutors\tutors-model-lib\src\utils\lo-utils.ts`, lines 22-33):
Recursively walks the tree. For each Lo, pushes it to results, then if it has a `los` property (i.e., is composite), recursively flattens those children too. Returns a flat array of all Los in the course.

### decorateCourseTree (from `D:\code\tutors\node_modules\@tutors\tutors-model-lib\src\services\lo-tree.ts`, lines 7-43):
1. Sets `courseId`, `courseUrl`, and `route` on the course
2. Flattens all Los and injects the course URL (replacing `{{COURSEURL}}` placeholders)
3. Removes unknown Los
4. Calls `decorateLoTree` recursively which:
   - Sets `parentCourse` on every Lo
   - Loads icon from frontMatter
   - Builds breadcrumbs
   - Converts markdown to HTML
   - For composite Los: extracts `panels` (panelVideos, panelTalks, panelNotes, podcasts) and `units` (units, sides, standardLos), builds `toc`, then recurses into children
5. Builds `loIndex` (Map of route -> Lo) and `topicIndex` (Map of route -> Topic)
6. Calls `loadPropertyFlags`, `createCompanions`, `createWalls`, `initCalendar`
